public_rationale: November 2023 GPT-4 text tests recorded both instruction-following successes and failures [e1]. A DALL-E 3 study conducted from March–November 2024 found recurring failures on negation prompts and improvement with prompt modification [e2]. Neither study measures the February 1–8, 2024 target period, so these results do not settle whether the systems discussed reliably fulfilled requests during that period [e1, e2].
limitations: The packet contains no qualifying independent repeated tests from the target period.
The exact system versions, prompt rewriting, and complete interactions behind the post's examples are unverified.
Image-generation results cannot establish reliability across language-model tasks.
The claim specifies neither a numerical reliability threshold nor a representative distribution of requests.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The large language model systems discussed in the post do not reliably deliver what they are asked for, even though clever, experienced users with time to spare can sometimes induce them to do something correctly.
conditions: the systems discussed in the post (large language models)
clever prompters with elaborate prompts can no doubt sometimes get correct results

statement.excerpt: The question is not whether a clever user with a lot of experience and time to kill can induce a mission to do something correctly, but whether the systems reliably deliver what they are asked for. They don’t.

from_speaker: whether the systems reliably deliver what they are asked for
a clever user with a lot of experience and time to kill
Compositionality remains a problem. So does negation.
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that the contemporary systems repeatedly fail straightforward requests without extensive prompting or retries. It is not that every request fails.
The surrounding examples concern image generation, especially composition and negation. Failures in an image-generation pipeline do not by themselves establish failures in every language-model task.
No numerical reliability threshold or representative task distribution is specified.

I use February 1–8, 2024, the publication month through the post date, as the latest observable period for this ongoing-state claim. The references to examples from last night and the author's current attempt anchor it to contemporary use.
The concession about clever prompting is not a conditional forecast or an antecedent that must occur before the observation can be assessed.
criteria.support_condition: Independent repeated tests of the systems operating in the target period show recurring failures to fulfill straightforward composition, negation, or comparable instructions without elaborate prompting. Isolated selected failures are insufficient.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Independent representative repeated tests of the same systems and relevant instructions show consistently correct fulfillment with ordinary prompts, and establish that the alleged recurring failures do not replicate.

evidence.locator: Section 3, Evaluation results, opening paragraph; Table 3 in the PDF
evidence.explanation: IFEval reports GPT-4 prompt-level accuracy of 76.89% under strict scoring and 79.30% under loose scoring, showing both substantial success and recurring failures. These are November 2023 text-generation tests, not measurements of the February 2024 image-generation pipeline.

evidence.publisher: arXiv; Colin Conwell, Rupert Tawiah-Quashie, and Tomer Ullman
evidence.explanation: The later study reports mean image–prompt agreement of 12.3% for unmodified negation prompts and 40.7% for modified prompts. This corroborates a related failure pattern and shows improvement from prompt modification, but its stated testing dates exclude the target period; the year-level event date summarizes that multi-month testing period.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Independent repeated tests from February 1–8, 2024 of the systems discussed, documenting versions, interfaces, prompts, complete outputs, attempt counts, and scoring rules. Tests should include successes and failures on straightforward composition, negation, or comparable instructions and distinguish ordinary prompts from automatic rewriting and elaborate manual prompting.
